episodes.165842: A marine thunderstorm wind gust was association with a late evening cold front.
episodes.165843: Showers and thunderstorms developed along and ahead of an evening cold front and produced a weak tornado and some hail.
episodes.166455: A strong shortwave trough traversed east across the Southern Plains during the afternoon and evening of March 14th, which reinforced a cold front southeast across Eastern Oklahoma, Western Arkansas, and North Texas during the afternoon and evening. A strong southerly low level flow allowed for low level moisture and increasing instability to return back north along a warm front, as it entered portions of Deep East Texas and the Lower Toledo Bend Country of Western Louisiana during the evening. Strong large scale forcing ahead of the approaching trough occurred along the cold front, allowing for a line of strong thunderstorms to develop and push east into East Texas during the mid and late evening. Isolated supercell thunderstorms also developed ahead of this line of storms over portions of Deep East Texas, and produced multiple instances of large hail over portions of Angelina, San Augustine, and Rusk Counties. These storms eventually weakened by late evening as they became more elevated and moved away from the waning instability away from the warm front.
episodes.167042: Thunderstorms developed in the warm, moist airmass ahead of a dryline. One of these storms produced large hail.
episodes.167140: A cold front crossed the area with strong thunderstorms that produced gusty winds.
episodes.167240: Strong to severe thunderstorms, which developed along a dryline and a Pacific cold front, affected areas mainly along and east of the Interstate 35 corridor during the afternoon and evening of Monday, March 14. Hail was the most frequent severe weather occurrence with these storms, but there was one confirmed tornado in Fannin County.
episodes.167526: A strong cold front came through southeast Louisiana on the night of March 15th. Strong low level convergence along this boundary combined with the deep layer forcing aloft aided in the development of severe thunderstorm winds over Lake Pontchartrain.
episodes.167716: An isolated thunderstorm along the coast produced a high wind gust near Port Arthur.

A very brief EF-0 tornado occurred along West Half Moon Road in Santa Fe, just to the northwest of Santa Fe High School. A large oak tree was snapped, causing roof damage and destroying a well pump. The garage door in a single family home was blown out. A utility building had its metal siding destroyed. Several large pieces of heavy equipment sitting outdoors were picked up and moved by the tornado.

The Weatherflow mesonet at Bayou Bienvenue measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 42 mph or 36 knots.
